description: Places MANY clips onto one sequence in a single round-trip — the fast path for rebuilding a whole edit (e.g. a Descript/EDL stringout). Equivalent to calling add_to_timeline (overwrite) once per clip, but ~50x faster because it loops inside one ExtendScript pass instead of one file round-trip per clip. Each clip supports per-clip linkAudio and sourceInPoint/sourceOutPoint (Source-monitor in/out). Returns a per-clip result array so one bad clip does not sink the batch, plus an aggregate status: top-level success is true ONLY when every clip placed; status is "success" | "partial" | "failure" with placed/failed/total counts.

clips.description: Ordered list of clips to place. All use overwrite mode.

linkAudio.description: When false, removes the auto-linked audio counterpart Premiere places on audio tracks for a video-track clip whose source carries an embedded audio stream (prevents overwriting existing audio in overlay/rebuild workflows). Default true (preserves Premiere's native linking).

projectItemId.description: The ID of the project item (clip / multicam) to add

sourceInPoint.description: Source IN point in seconds (requires sourceOutPoint)

sourceOutPoint.description: Source OUT point in seconds (requires sourceInPoint)

time.description: Timeline position in seconds where the clip is placed (overwrite). Required in "absolute" mode; ignored in "append" mode.

trackIndex.description: The index of the video or audio track (0-based)

mode.description: Placement mode. "absolute" (default) uses each clip's time. "append" ignores time and lays clips end-to-end with NO gaps: each clip on a given track starts exactly where the previous one ends (seeded from that track's existing content), chained off the placed clip's real frame-aligned end so float-second rounding cannot open a 1-frame gap. Use append to rebuild a continuous stringout.

sequenceId.description: The ID of the sequence (timeline) to add clips to. Defaults to the active sequence.

name: add_to_timeline_batch
